newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PM SEES BANKS RELEASING FUNDS FOR BAD DEBTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PM SEES BANKS RELEASING FUNDS FOR BAD DEBTS.

text.p: The Slovak government expects domestic banks to release some 30 billion crowns from their reserves by the end of this year to help pay off bad debts, the official news agency TASR reported late on Saturday.

"Banks already hold about 30 billion crowns in the form of provisions for bad loans, and the government expects these funds to be released by the end of the year to help pay off their debts," TASR quoted Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar as saying.

"This sum is already in the banks but, at present, there is no mechanism that would release the money for such purpose," Meciar said after an extraodinary meeting of Slovak economic ministers in Trencianske Teplice, central Slovakia.
He added the government was negotiating with the banks on a compromise solution for releasing the funds.
Neither Meciar, nor any other cabinet member would elaborate further on the plan. TASR said.
